correctness.rationale: For n>=2 the centered-square generators are a=2n²-2n+1,b=2n²+2n+1,c=2n²+6n+5. Adjacent pair gcds are one and gcd(a,c)=gcd(5,2n+1), so only n=2 mod5 can have a nontrivial gluing. At n=2, c=25=5a and <5,13> has F=47, genus24, type1. For n>=3 c cannot lie in <a,b>, checked by sizes for n>=6 and explicit n=3..5, so the triple is minimal. For n not 2 mod5 the Watanabe–Herzog gluing criterion excludes symmetry. For n=5k+2, k>=2, a/5=A=10k²+6k+1, c/5=C=10k²+14k+5, b=B=50k²+50k+13: 4C<B<6A forces x+y=5 in B=xA+yC, hence y=2+k/(2k+1) nonintegral. For k=1, 113=17x+29y has no nonnegative solution by residue and size. Thus n>=3 nonsymmetric, and standard 3-generator type dichotomy gives type2. Independently computed 39 exact Apéry sets for n=2..40, all agreeing; finite calculation is corroboration only. Domain and generalized criterion premises were separately checked.
